scope: Fourth fingerprint optimization round: native permission/geolocation contracts, effective privacy policy and storage estimates

findings.changes: Remove synthetic Permissions.query and PermissionStatus.state overrides. The browser owns dictionary conversion, validation, native states and status objects; no post-query descriptor reads occur.

Remove fake getCurrentPosition/watchPosition denial callbacks; retain native receiver/callback/options validation, real watch IDs, cancellation and genuine native error objects. Chromium native grant and denial setup is mandatory before script registration.

evidence: geoMode disabled formerly left effective permission at prompt when geoPermission was absent
Firefox 160 native probe: permissions.default.geo=2 plus an existing geolocation grant still returned permission granted and attempted native position access
Firefox geo.enabled=false removes native geolocation even for granted origins
changes: Resolve disabled mode as denied even without an explicit deny selector; retain deny for allow without valid coordinates
Firefox writes geo.enabled false for effective denial, true for prompt/allow, and one matching default permission value
Apply native BiDi grants/denials to managed HTTP(S) startup origins before navigation, cache only successful setup and propagate failures
Share one estimate patch between documents, same-origin child realms and workers
Delegate receiver/argument validation to the original native method, accepting genuine foreign-realm managers
Keep the actual native dictionary, its realm, property flags, optional absence and additional members
Bound any adjusted quota by the quota returned in that call; consider existing usage without inventing extra native capacity
Recognize an existing same-token patch to avoid wrapper stacking
Isolate the VM storage fixture class and intrinsics instead of modifying shared host Function/Object prototypes

chromiumChecks: Stock and injected descriptor getter/coercion counts, frozen dictionaries and forged receivers
Missing callbacks, forged receivers and throwing options retain native errors
Positive watch IDs, genuine errors with no synthetic own fields, and native clearWatch cancellation
Storage quota bounds, optional members and borrowed-call result realms in the main document and same-origin iframe
Storage/permission behavior in dedicated, shared and service workers
Native granted (0,0) position and untouched-realm comparison under Permissions-Policy restrictions
firefoxChecks: Deny-mode first-script native permission setup overrides a pre-existing origin grant
An unprepared, separately authorized origin still has no native geolocation API in deny mode
The same persisted profile restores geolocation in allow mode and returns configured (0,0)
Storage result shape, native quota bound, result realm and foreign receivers
Gecko permission conversion counts match its own untouched sandbox
unitChecks: Native brand validation and genuine foreign receivers
Mandatory Chromium denial failure blocks registration
Firefox permission setup precedes navigation and failures are not cached
referenceNotes: The first aggregate run had one obsolete coverage check that treated any navigator.storage text as mutation. It was replaced with execution of the complete emitted script, preserving manager/persistence identity and verifying that the bounded estimate patch actually ran; the final aggregate run uses this corrected check

Chromium quota includes current origin usage; cached injected Service Worker bytes change total quota. Worker regression comparisons therefore use available space, with the corresponding stock worker scope as reference

Under an explicit CDP grant and restrictive Permissions-Policy, Chrome 157 returned permission state granted but blocked location access with code 1 in both injected and untouched realms. The test preserves observed native behavior instead of assuming query must say denied

behaviorChanges: Existing profiles with geoMode disabled and no explicit deny now receive effective native denial
Firefox deny mode deliberately has native absence of navigator.geolocation; prompt/allow launches restore the feature
Affected live quota readings can decrease to the actual native bound; saved seeds and the 240 default V1 replay fixtures remain unchanged
Unsupported required native permission commands reject setup/navigation rather than reporting simulated success
remainingLimits: Native Windows/macOS kernels and platform-specific driver/font behavior are not certified on Linux
Firefox native grants are prepared for managed startup origins; arbitrary redirect destinations, subsequent script-driven origins and cross-origin frames retain their native permission behavior
The storage reporting ceiling does not replace native allocation/persistence enforcement or synthesize a disk of the reported size
Firefox cached/blob/data/local-bypass Worker first-instruction and native Gecko transport limits remain documented
No claim of perfect or universally indistinguishable browser emulation
